events.text: Born in Bishop Burton, Yorkshire, England.

evidence.quote: In 1854 he joined the Church Missionary Society ( CMS ) and attended the Church Missionary Society College , Islington

events.text: Sent by the CMS to the North Pacific coast of Canada.

evidence.quote: In 1856 the CMS sent Duncan to the North Pacific coast of Canada

events.text: Arrived at the HBC fort settlement at Lax Kwalaams, British Columbia.

evidence.quote: and in 1857 he arrived at the remote Hudsons Bay Company ( HBC ) fort settlement at Lax Kwalaams , British Columbia

events.label: founding
events.text: Metlakatla officially established as a utopian Christian community in British Columbia.

evidence.quote: Metlakatla was officially established that year within what was by then the Colony of British Columbia

events.text: Expelled from the Church Missionary Society.

evidence.quote: Duncan was expelled from the CMS in 1881 and transformed his mission into a nondenominational Independent Native Church

events.text: Transformed his mission into a nondenominational Independent Native Church.

events.text: Led about 800 Tsimshians by canoe from Old Metlakatla to New Metlakatla, Alaska.

evidence.quote: in a canoe voyage from Old Metlakatla to New Metlakatla , Alaska , in 1887

events.text: Interior Department began seizing many of the Metlakatla mission buildings.

evidence.quote: In 1914–1915 , the Interior Department seized many of the Mission buildings and built a modern school at Metlakatla

events.label: death
events.text: Died at age 86 in New Metlakatla, Alaska.

evidence.quote: Duncan died at the age of 86 on 30 August 1918

undated_mentions: Later worked as a tanner in his grandfather's/adoptive father's trade
